newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet firms on prompt squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet firms on prompt squeeze.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel swaps were firm late afternoon on Tuesday on tight prompt supplies and strong demand by traders looking to cover earlier sales to North Asia, market sources said.

December jet fuel swaps traded this morning to a high of $33.45 per barrel and this afternoon at about $33.30, brokers said. The market was last quoted at $33.20/$33.40 a barrel, up from Monday's $32.80/$33.20.
However, the December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) was quoted slightly lower at $2.40/$2.60, down from Monday's $2.60/$2.80 due to the higher gas oil values, brokers said.
The recent surge in jet fuel prices was due to traders covering earlier sale commitments to North Asia, industry sources said.

December gas oil swaps remained firm and traded to an intraday high of $30.93 before edging down slightly to $30.80/$30.85, brokers said. It also traded at $30.85 and $30.80 earlier today, up from late Monday's $30.65/$30.75.

The rise comes despite the overnight fall to January Brent crude futures in London by 41 cents a barrel to $22.61 on news Iraq had agreed to all the conditions for the United Nations oil-for-food deal.
Gas oil futures, traded in London, also lost ground on Monday and December futures dropped $3.75 a tonne to $219.00. It opened on Tuesday down $1.50 a tonne to $217.50.
The Asian gas oil market is supported by increased buying from China and other regional buyers, such as Indonesia, traders said.

Naphtha remained weak due to the lower crude values with December quoted last quoted at $23.30/$23.50. But traders said naphtha fundamentals were strong compared to gasoline, pressuring the light distillate spread to around $2.00. Gasoline December swaps were bid/asked at $25.30/$25.50.
Fuel oil was quoted unchanged from earlier Tuesday in quiet trade with December was last quoted at $120.00/$121.00.
